neighbours.label: a word judging whether a format, value or syntax is admissible (valid / acceptable / legal / allowed / permitted / malformed) in talk about data formats and language rules; not 'valid until' or a 'legitimate reason'
fire: The field must contain a valid date in the form YYYY-MM-DD.
Other acceptable formats include CSV and plain text.
An empty list is a perfectly legal argument to this function.
The checker flags any malformed header in the file.
Only letters and digits are allowed in a username.
Both 24-hour and 12-hour times are valid formats for this column.
The function tests whether the string is a valid hexadecimal number.
Spaces are not permitted values for the key name.
quiet: The field must contain a date in the form YYYY-MM-DD.
Other common formats include CSV and plain text.
An empty list is passed as the argument to this function.
The checker reads every header in the file.
Only letters and digits appear in her username.
Her driving licence is valid until the end of next year.
The function converts the string into a hexadecimal number.
He gave a legitimate excuse for missing the meeting.

notes: Probes ran 0.2-0.45 of max on format-validity words and ~0 on 'valid until' / 'legitimate reason'. Two near misses test the word without the format sense.
